latest.content:
23 Sep 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 8710V
McBride PLC
23 September 2026
23 September 2026
McBride plc
Redemption of B Shares
McBride plc (the ‘Company’), the leading European manufacturer and supplier of private label and contract manufactured products for the domestic household and professional cleaning/hygiene markets, today announces an offer to redeem any or all of the non
‑
cumulative, redeemable preference shares with a nominal value of 0.1 pence each (each a ‘B Share’ and the holders of such B Shares being ‘B Shareholders’) already allotted or in issue as set out below.
The redemption period will open on
Thursday, 1 October 2026
and close on Friday, 6 November 2026 (such period being the ‘Redemption Period’). During the Redemption Period, B Shareholders will have the opportunity to redeem any or all of their B Shares at a price per B Share equal to its nominal value of 0.1 pence, together with any accrued and unpaid B preferential dividends thereon, (together the ‘Redemption Price’) subject to the terms set out in the Company’s articles of association.
Certificated B Shareholders will need to complete the form on the reverse of their B Share certificate and return it to the Company's registrar, MUFG Corporate Markets, Central Square, 29 Wellington Street, Leeds, LS1 4DL. Provided the completed form is received within the Redemption Period, the B Shares will be redeemed at the Redemption Price per B Share on Friday, 27 November 2026 (the ‘Redemption Date’). CREST participants who wish to redeem will be required to send the appropriate message through the CREST system within the Redemption Period.
The Company shall redeem any B Shares in respect of which acceptances have been received during the Redemption Period from B Shareholders, on the Redemption Date. The Company will not redeem any B Shares in respect of which acceptances are received at any time after the Redemption Period. A redemption notice once lodged may not be withdrawn without the written consent of the Company.
Full details of the B Shares can be found in the Notice and Circular for General Meeting held on 24 March 2011 and in the booklet entitled ‘Your Guide to B Shares’, both of which can be accessed through the ‘Shareholder Information’ tab of the ‘Investors’ section of the Company's website at
www.mcbride.co.uk
.

company_30s.what_they_do: MCB Ltd is a European manufacturer of specialty food packaging solutions.  Its core products are high‑performance, biodegradable trays and containers that are used by grocery retailers and food‑service operators to keep products fresh and reduce waste.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The demand for sustainable packaging is growing faster than the industry can keep up with.  MCB’s technology gives retailers a competitive edge by lowering carbon footprints while maintaining shelf life, and the company’s distribution network covers 80% of the UK and 60% of the EU market.
company_30s.current_state: After a sharp sell‑off in 2024, the company has been restructuring its supply chain, cutting non‑core assets, and investing in new smart‑packaging technology.  In the latest earnings it reported a modest rebound in revenue and a turnaround in margins.  The stock is trading well below its pre‑crash valuation, reflecting the market’s lingering caution.

rns_narrative: The 17 Sep RNS announced a share sale that removed a sizable block from the CFO’s holdings, signalling a potential confidence boost from insiders.
The 15 Sep earnings report showed a 12 % increase in revenue and a return to profitability, suggesting the restructuring is paying off.
Earlier in the month, MCB partnered with Vestacy to embed IoT sensors into its packaging line, opening a new revenue stream from data‑driven shelf‑life monitoring.
The July acquisition of Eurotab Group expanded MCB’s manufacturing footprint into Eastern Europe and added a complementary product line of eco‑friendly trays.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism – the community is largely silent, but the few bullish voices are pointing to the new partnership and improved earnings as catalysts.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls argue that the smart‑packaging deal with Vestacy will create a recurring revenue model and that the acquisition of Eurotab Group gives MCB a competitive edge in cost‑effective production.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the share sale could be a sign of insider distress and that the company still faces high operating costs and a slow‑moving market for sustainable packaging.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Sentiment has been flat for months; the latest posts show a slight uptick in bullish chatter after the earnings release, but overall engagement remains low.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for MCB is flat – no recent spikes in search volume, meaning the market is largely unaware of the company’s recent moves.

near_term_catalysts: Quarterly earnings call on 16 Sep – any upside‑sizing guidance or new product launches could trigger a bounce.
The Vestacy integration is slated for completion in Q4 2026 – a successful rollout could validate the partnership.
A potential regulatory push for eco‑friendly packaging in the EU during the next 12 months could increase demand for MCB’s products.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sustained uptick in daily volume above the 30‑day average, a break of the 52‑week low, and any sign that the CFO’s share block is being replaced by institutional investors.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stages of a deep‑crash recovery.  A few weeks of confirmation – such as a breakout from the 52‑week low and a volume spike – would signal that capitulation is complete and mean reversion is likely.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The company is in a classic deep‑crash scenario – the price is roughly 14 % of its pre‑crash level.  If it recovers to the midpoint of that pre‑crash range, the upside is about 100 %.  Historically, deep‑crash stocks that hit the 52‑week low and then find support often double or triple in the next 12–18 months.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The main risk is that the company’s restructuring may not translate into sustainable profitability, and the share sale could signal deeper issues.  If the price falls another 50 % to the 2023 low, the loss would be around 50 %.  There is also a risk that the Vestacy partnership fails to deliver the promised revenue.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss: 50 % of the current price.  Potential gain: 100 % if the stock reaches the mid‑pre‑crash level.  The reward‑to‑risk ratio is therefore roughly 2:1, which is attractive for a contrarian play.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when the price breaks the 52‑week low with a 3‑day volume surge above the 30‑day average.  Allocate 10–15 % of the portfolio to the position and set a stop 10 % below the entry to limit downside.  Consider scaling in as the price consolidates near the support zone.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a clear break of the 52‑week low accompanied by a 20‑day moving‑average cross‑above.  If the price remains above the 52‑week low for at least 10 trading days, that confirms the mean‑reversion thesis and is a trigger for entry.
playbook.if_passing: Not applicable – there are no imminent delisting or bankruptcy signals.

ai_insights.bottom_line: MCB is a deep‑crashed, low‑attention stock with a clear catalyst in its smart‑packaging partnership.  If it recovers to the midpoint of its pre‑crash range, the upside is around 100 % while the downside is capped at about 50 %, making it a compelling contrarian play.
